structure_flags.label: Theorem 2 / proposal headline
structure_flags.one_line: The strongest novel kernel is a still-to-prove theorem rather than a conjecture; relabel the headline result as a conjecture while retaining its coupled construction.

novelty_flags.label: related_work and bibliography: lin2026statistical
novelty_flags.one_line: The proposal calls Lin et al. (2026) an AISTATS proceeding, but the verified source is public arXiv preprint 2602.20681; retain its randomized-design comparison but correct its source status.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 2 / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Fixed overlap, compact smooth bounded arm densities, strong conditional Brenier regularity, and sigma_n>=sigma_star are accepted as regular-regime restrictions; equality and vanishing-variance sequences are excluded.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The claimed efficiency, uniform studentized normality, and Wald coverage are conditional on the stated regular observed-law class, while the equality frontier remains the separate open-ended question.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Relabel the main regular-inference result as a conjecture and state explicitly that its coupled fitted-kernel construction is the proposed route to proving the displayed quadratic-plus-product remainder.
Correct Lin et al. (2026) to arXiv:2602.20681 and distinguish its completely randomized design from observational ignorability in a compact comparison table.
Turn the degeneracy handle into a specified local conditional-law perturbation family and candidate second-order statistic or resampling functional.

recommended_next_step: Revise the headline theorem into a conjecture and correct the Lin et al. source-status comparison, then rerun this field-tier review.
